violations.title: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY missing
violations.message: Table public.swap_offers has RLS enabled but not FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The table owner role still bypasses RLS, which often masks broken policies in development and CI. Run `ALTER TABLE public.swap_offers FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;`.

violations.title: Permissive policy grants access to PUBLIC
violations.message: Permissive policy 'browse offers' on public.swap_offers grants access to PUBLIC, so anonymous connections are governed by this policy's own clause — its USING for reads, its WITH CHECK for writes (a FOR INSERT policy has no USING at all). Restrict to a specific role (e.g. TO authenticated).

violations.title: Policy expression does not reference any column of the table
violations.message: Policy 'browse offers' on public.swap_offers does not reference any column of the table. The predicate is purely session-state — every row is admitted or denied based on configuration alone. Add a row-level condition (e.g. tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant')).

violations.title: All policies on table are permissive
violations.message: Every policy on public.swap_offers is permissive. Permissive policies combine with OR — adding one RESTRICTIVE policy gives a floor (e.g. tenant scoping) that no OR branch can bypass, for the roles in its own TO list. Use TO PUBLIC to bind every role: measured, a restrictive TO authenticated left authenticated at 1 row and another role at 3.

violations.title: Permissive policy USING clause is constant true
violations.message: Policy 'browse offers' on public.swap_offers has USING (true), which admits every row to every caller in the role list. Replace with a real predicate or remove the policy.

violations.title: Anonymous read leak (USING is unconditionally true for an unauthenticated session)
violations.message: Policy 'browse offers' on public.swap_offers leaks every row to an anonymous session. Under an unauthenticated connection every auth function (auth.uid(), auth.role(), current_setting(), …) returns NULL, and Z3 proves the USING predicate is then unconditionally TRUE for every row (three-valued / Kleene logic) — so the policy reads all rows. Every row is visible unconditionally (the predicate is constant-true under anon — it pins no row column). Gate the policy on a non-null auth check (e.g. `auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND <tenant/owner check>`) or remove the inverting disjunct that admits anonymous. This is the semantic form of the SEC004 inverted-auth hole — see SEC004 for the syntactic variant.

violations.title: PostgREST-exposed table readable by a low-trust role
violations.message: Table public.swap_offers is in the PostgREST-exposed schema public, grants SELECT to anon, authenticated, and has no effective row filter (RLS is enabled but only a permissive USING (true) policy, which admits every row) — it is directly readable at GET /rest/v1/swap_offers by an unauthenticated or any-authenticated request. Enable RLS with a row-scoping policy (or restrict/REVOKE the grant); if the table is intentionally public, allowlist 'public.swap_offers' in [lint.rules.SEC049]. (SEC001/SEC003/SEC008 each flag a precondition of this in isolation; SEC049 is the conjunction.)

violations.title: Auth function called per-row in policy USING/WITH CHECK
violations.message: Policy 'post offer' on public.swap_offers calls an auth function in WITH CHECK without wrapping it in a subquery. Postgres re-evaluates the call per row. Wrap as e.g. (SELECT auth.uid()) so the planner caches the result for the whole statement.

violations.title: Auth function called per-row in policy USING/WITH CHECK
violations.message: Policy 'claim or edit offer' on public.swap_offers calls an auth function in USING and WITH CHECK without wrapping it in a subquery. Postgres re-evaluates the call per row. Wrap as e.g. (SELECT auth.uid()) so the planner caches the result for the whole statement.
